title: ASCII Kinesis V2 Strikes014 — Offhand Countertorque Impact Debt

principle.pocket: IMPACT TORQUE CAN BE PAID BY THE NON-STRIKING SIDE BEFORE THE STRIKING LIMB RECOVERS.
principle.causal_thesis: A committed diagonal implement strike reaches contact before terminal reach. At impact, the contralateral hand/shoulder catches rotational debt while the pelvis and lead support absorb remaining forward momentum. The implement overshoots after contact, then root recoil leads while the tool and offhand repay different lag debts before displaced re-entry.
principle.novelty_vs_canonical_003_013: Moves impact debt across the contralateral/offhand channel rather than routing it only through the striking limb, tool constraint, root overrun, force-axis redirection, projectile clock, or clearance problem.

source.name: Cress Albane
observed: Campaign evidence records the complete 696x834 PNG sheet as inspected.
Whole-sheet families include Idle, Guard, Damaged, Dead, Knocked Out & Getting Up, Walk, Run & Stop, multiple attack families, swordless variants, and separate sword/shield graphics.
The sheet establishes separable body/equipment/action families but does not establish playback exposure.
inferred: All Strikes014 pose geometry, contact point, target plane, implement path, offhand countertorque behavior, support sequence, recovery logic, and compile cadence are independently authored abstractions.
Contralateral/offhand torque capture is a synthetic transferable strike principle, not source choreography.

keys.name: OFFSET_READY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root starts left of target with lead foot forward; offhand occupies forward negative space.
keys.causal_role: Readable asymmetric baseline; striking hand is rear/low and offhand is forward/high.

keys.name: REAR_COIL
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root shifts back/down one cell while chest counter-rotates; rear foot owns load.
keys.causal_role: Specific asymmetrical coil: striking side winds behind pelvis while offhand reaches forward as counterweight.

keys.name: COUNTERWIND_LOAD
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Pelvis stays back as chest rises; implement head climbs while offhand remains long.
keys.causal_role: Separates offhand counterweight from strike hand load before directional commitment.

keys.name: DIAGONAL_ENTRY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root advances first; lead foot opens and chest follows one beat behind.
keys.causal_role: Root earns the strike before the implement closes the target line.

keys.name: PRECONTACT_GAP
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Lead support accepts weight while root still travels; implement tip holds a visible two-cell gap.
keys.causal_role: Distinct precontact silhouette; no target contact yet and contact is not terminal reach.

keys.name: IMPACT
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root advances only one cell into contact; lead leg braces and torso continues to wind.
keys.causal_role: Explicit contact instant/hold before farthest implement reach. Offhand begins crossing inward to catch torque.

keys.name: OFFHAND_COUNTERTORQUE_CATCH
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root/chest overrun slightly forward while offhand crosses the torso opposite the strike.
keys.causal_role: Contralateral hand crosses the sternum and clamps on the striking side, visibly catching rotational debt while the implement overshoots.

keys.name: TORSION_OVERSHOOT
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Pelvis drops into lead support; chest yaw passes the pelvis while implement tip drifts high/right.
keys.causal_role: Cross-body clamp survives the implement's high/right overshoot; tool and offhand now carry different post-impact debts.

keys.name: ROOT_RECOIL_LEADS
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root begins retreat before the implement; torso comes back while tip remains extended.
keys.causal_role: Pelvis/root recoil leads while the offhand remains cross-body and the implement remains long; neither secondary channel reverse-interpolates.

keys.name: IMPLEMENT_LAG_REPAY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Support widens; tool finally trails back while offhand still guards the torque channel.
keys.causal_role: Secondary lag moves from root to implement; negative space reopens unevenly.

keys.name: OFFHAND_RELEASE_LAG
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root is stable but offhand releases later than the implement, preserving contralateral debt.
keys.causal_role: Offhand is the last major body channel to unwind; it does not mirror the initial reach.

keys.name: SUPPORT_RESTACK_DISPLACED
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Rear foot steps under a root that remains forward of the starting address.
keys.causal_role: Support catches remaining torque without returning to the original stance.

keys.name: SECONDARY_SETTLE
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Chest settles past root then recenters; tool tip makes a small delayed downward settle.
keys.causal_role: Small authored overshoot/settle prevents a hard snap to ready.

keys.name: DISPLACED_REENTRY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Ready returns three to four cells forward of K00 with a narrower rear-side implement pocket.
keys.causal_role: Recovery debt is paid at a new address; silhouette echoes readiness without resetting to idle.

quality_history.highest_value_visible_defect: The offhand countertorque catch reads as a small inward tuck, not a decisive contralateral torque-capture action; the specimen's new causal thesis is visually underperformed.
quality_history.concrete_same_body_correction: Push K06/K07 offhand clearly across the sternum to the striking side, hold that cross-body clamp through torsion overshoot, then let K08/K09 release it later than root recoil so the offhand debt is visibly separate from tool debt.

quality_history.visible_judgment: Cross-body offhand clamp now reads as a separate post-contact torque sink: K05 impact remains before terminal reach; K06/K07 preserve implement overshoot while the offhand crosses and holds; K08 root recoil leads both secondary debts; K09–K13 repay implement then offhand/support debt into displaced re-entry.

quality_history.judgment: The performance has an opinion: the offhand is not decoration. It reaches as counterweight, snaps across after impact, stays clamped while the implement overshoots, then releases on its own debt clock. The displaced re-entry refuses a polite reset.
